I ran all 14 queries. Each gave a sensible result on the sample files, but I only checked a few by hand.

- **Checked by hand:** T13 matches the CSV. Acme is 25 + 4×19.99 = 104.96, and Birch is 59.97 + 50 = 109.97.
- **Output shape:** For T3, T7 and T10, qlang keeps map keys as keywords, so the printed keys are `:db`, `:api` and so on. T13 prints `{:customer … :total …}` records.
- **T10:** It tests the level token itself, not a substring match.

T1: /data/users | filter ~(allOf /active (at :email | coalesce "" | lower | endsWith "@example.com")) | count
T2: /data/users | filter ~(/roles | map ~(lower) | contains "admin") | sort ~(/name | lower) | map ~(/name)
T3: /data/users | groupBy ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :country | coalesce "unknown") | map ~(count)
T4: /data/users | map ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2
T5: / | filter ~(/state | eq "open") | map ~(/labels | map ~(/name | lower)) | flat | distinct | sort
T6: / | sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 | map ~({:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | coalesce null | if (eq null) ~(null) ~(/login))})
T7: / | filter ~(allOf (/state | eq "open") (at :assignee | ne null)) | groupBy ~(/assignee/login) | map ~(count)
T8: :dev /devDependencies | /dependencies | union dev | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) | map ~([(/0 | print | drop 1) (/1)] | join "@")
T9: /services | filter ~(allOf (at :enabled | eq true) (/port | gt 8000)) | map ~(/name | lower) | sort | join ","
T10: lines | map ~(split " ") | filter ~(at 1 | eq "ERROR") | map ~(at 2) | groupBy ~(/) | map ~(count)
T11: lines | map ~(split " " | filter ~(startsWith "ms=") | map ~(drop 3 | parseJson)) | flat | avg | round 1
T12: lines | drop 1 | map ~(split ",") | filter ~(allOf (/4 | ne "") (/5 | lower | eq "shipped")) | map ~(mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum | round 2
T13: lines | drop 1 | map ~(split ",") | filter ~(allOf (/4 | ne "") (/5 | lower | ne "cancelled")) | groupBy ~(/1) | map ~(map ~(mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum) | entries | map ~({:customer (/0 | print | drop 1) :total (/1 | round 2)}) | sort ~([(/total | desc)]) | take 2
